title: CLAUDE.md
text: Entry point: inla_vanilla(logpost, init, grad = NULL, ..., vb = TRUE, verbose = TRUE, control = list()) R/inla-vanilla.R. optim() nlminb(), dots come gradient, vb, verbose control must named full data arguments partially match . Input. user supplies single logpost(theta, ...) unconstrained scale ϑ ∈ ℝᵐ, Jacobian already included; ... passed optim(). transform layer v1. Natural-scale derived quantities come sampling(fit, fun = ...). later transform layer planned wrapper builds unconstrained logpost unchanged engine (see lab/DESIGN.md), keep engine free transform logic. Wrappers. inla_vanilla() binds ... logpost_x() grad_x(), wraps closures (lp, gr) name parameters, count calls, record last parameter value tick progress. Every stage receives closures, never user functions. Never forward ... internal helpers, user’s data argument partially match one formals (applies fun sampling()). with_context() reports error logpost grad stage parameter value. stages run order, one file : mode comes nlminb. whitened gradient mode still 1e-3, nlminb reruns scale = sqrt(diag(H)). Finite-difference steps set per coordinate fd_scales(), cheap curvature search. gradient Hessian takes central differences 1e-4 scale; without one, fd_hessian() 0.01 . keeps posterior SDs 1e-6 1e4 working. returns R (upper Cholesky precision), Σ, L (L Lᵀ = Σ), whitened gradient mode (, nlminb’s return code, decides convergence warning), Jacobian asymmetry (check user grad), Laplace log marginal likelihood. vb_correct() INLAvaan’s fixed-point iteration Anderson(1) acceleration nlminb fallback. Gaussian expectation uses vb_nodes(), fully symmetric degree-5 cubature rule (2m²+1 nodes Σ’s principal axes). replaced INLAvaan’s Sobol points benchmark lab/vb-benchmark.R. fit$logml = Laplace + ½ δᵀHδ. parameter scanned seq(-4, 4) posterior SDs along conditional mode path, corrected gamma1_*, fitted fit_skew_normal(). volume correction two routes must agree: gamma1_grad() INLAvaan’s shortcut, using gradient; gamma1_lp() uses second differences logpost gradient, O(m) calls per parameter instead O(m²). marginals scanned around mode ϑ*, VB move . scan_bend() computes diagnostic bend: log-density, nats, straight scan misses ±2 SDs, one Newton step parameters. summary() flags 0.1. catches documented small-n narrowing. scan fixed ±4 SDs, INLAvaan. tails records scan whose ends stay log_threshold. Extending scan heavy tails tried rejected, hurt fit cases. Copula draws (R/sampling.R). sampling() S3 generic, matching INLAvaan’s exported sampling(). Draws go sn_score_map(), spline normal scores skew-normal quantiles; use qsnorm_fast() directly, starting value, accurate 5e-2. Supporting files: Skew-normal utilities (R/skew-normal.R, R/qsnorm-fast.R): ported INLAvaan. Apache-licensed qsnorm_fast() keeps attribution header. internal. Methods (R/methods.R): print() summary() print via cli::cat_* stdout. Progress (R/progress.R): stage cli progress bar appears 0.5 s, ends plain styled message() line. cli’s glue-based helpers (cli_progress_step(), cli_alert_*()) cost several ms per call, much whole small fit, avoid fitting path. Errors warnings: raise abort() warn() (R/utils.R), format cli signal base R, giving classes inlavanilla_error inlavanilla_warning. use cli::cli_abort() cli::cli_warn(): call rlang, cli suggests. Non-ASCII output: user-visible non-ASCII characters (σ, ·) go sd_unit() sep_dot(), fall back ASCII. R source files must stay ASCII. scope v0.1: factor scores, PPP/DIC/LOO/WAIC, multiple chains, compiled code, INLAvaan’s alternative methods (marginal types, NORTA, optimisers, Sobol Gauss–Hermite VB, parallel cores). add alternative methods; one method per stage.

code: library(inlavanilla)  X <- cbind(1, scale(mtcars$wt), scale(mtcars$hp)) y <- mtcars$am coef(summary(glm(am ~ scale(wt) + scale(hp), binomial, data = mtcars))) #>              Estimate Std. Error   z value    Pr(>|z|) #> (Intercept) -1.822019   1.091908 -1.668657 0.095185417 #> scale(wt)   -7.909336   3.002568 -2.634191 0.008433813 #> scale(hp)    2.485788   1.215904  2.044394 0.040914646 logpost <- function(theta, X, y) {   eta <- as.numeric(X %*% theta)   sum(dbinom(y, 1, plogis(eta), log = TRUE)) +     sum(dnorm(theta, 0, 2.5, log = TRUE)) } init <- c(b0 = 0, b_wt = 0, b_hp = 0) fit <- inla_vanilla(logpost, init, X = X, y = y) #> ✔ Found the posterior mode in 10 iterations [7ms] #> ✔ VB mean correction, max shift 0.43σ [17ms] #> ✔ Fitted 3 skew-normal marginals [9ms] fit #> ── INLAvanilla ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── 40ms ── #> 3 parameters · skew-normal marginals · VB-corrected #>  #>         Mean     SD    2.5%     50%  97.5%    Mode #> b0    -1.104  0.615  -2.398  -1.072  0.017  -1.008 #> b_wt   -5.12   1.35   -8.00   -5.03  -2.72   -4.85 #> b_hp   1.564  0.704   0.306   1.518  3.069   1.423 #>  #> Log marginal likelihood: -11.62 summary(fit) #> ── INLAvanilla summary ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>  #> Posterior marginals #>         Mean     SD    2.5%     25%     50%     75%  97.5%    Mode #> b0    -1.104  0.615  -2.398  -1.497  -1.072  -0.678  0.017  -1.008 #> b_wt   -5.12   1.35   -8.00   -5.97   -5.03   -4.18  -2.72   -4.85 #> b_hp   1.564  0.704   0.306   1.073   1.518   2.008  3.069   1.423 #>  #> Diagnostics #>       VB shift  SN - VB  Shape    NMAD   Bend #> b0       -0.13   0.0084   -1.5  0.0091   0.14 #> b_wt     -0.43   -0.057   -1.7   0.017   0.05 #> b_hp      0.26    0.076    1.7  0.0049  0.024 #>  #> ✔ Mode found in 10 iterations (gradient 2.2e-07 SDs). #> ✔ VB correction in 4 iterations: max shift 0.43 SDs. #> ! The straight scan misses up to 0.14 nats at +-2 SDs for b0: the marginal may be too narrow. #> ✔ Skew-normal fits: max NMAD 0.017. #> ✔ Skew-normal and VB means agree to within 0.076 SDs. #>  #> Log marginal likelihood: -11.615 (Laplace -11.709, VB term 0.094) #> 511 logpost calls in 40ms (mode 7ms, VB 18ms, marginals 9ms) plot(fit)

title: Get started with inlavanilla
text: three parameters can afford exact posterior brute force: log-posterior fine grid, normalised numerically. reference approximations trying match. 2.5%, 50% 97.5% quantiles exact posterior, skew-normal marginals Laplace Gaussian: skew-normal intervals track exact ones closely. intercept’s little narrow, bend flag warned. Laplace intervals symmetric mode, cut long tails short miss values far side. grid also gives exact log marginal likelihood: VB correction moves Laplace estimate way exact value.
code: s <- fit$summary axes <- lapply(seq_len(3), function(j) {   seq(s[j, "Mean"] - 7 * s[j, "SD"], s[j, "Mean"] + 7 * s[j, "SD"], length.out = 61) }) grid <- as.matrix(expand.grid(axes)) eta <- X %*% t(grid) lp <- colSums(y * eta - log1p(exp(eta))) +   rowSums(dnorm(grid, 0, 2.5, log = TRUE)) w <- exp(lp - max(lp))  # Exact marginal quantiles, by the midpoint rule on each axis exact_quantiles <- function(j, probs) {   p <- tapply(w, grid[, j], sum)   p <- as.numeric(p) / sum(p)   approx(cumsum(p) - p / 2, axes[[j]], probs, ties = mean)$y } probs <- c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975) compare <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(3), function(j) {   rbind(     exact = exact_quantiles(j, probs),     `skew-normal` = s[j, c("2.5%", "50%", "97.5%")],     Laplace = qnorm(probs, fit$mode[j], sqrt(fit$cov[j, j]))   ) })) rownames(compare) <- paste(rep(names(init), each = 3), rownames(compare)) colnames(compare) <- c("2.5%", "50%", "97.5%") round(compare, 2) #>                   2.5%   50% 97.5% #> b0 exact         -2.47 -1.08  0.08 #> b0 skew-normal   -2.40 -1.07  0.02 #> b0 Laplace       -2.22 -1.03  0.16 #> b_wt exact       -7.89 -5.00 -2.68 #> b_wt skew-normal -8.00 -5.03 -2.72 #> b_wt Laplace     -6.97 -4.51 -2.05 #> b_hp exact        0.25  1.50  3.04 #> b_hp skew-normal  0.31  1.52  3.07 #> b_hp Laplace      0.09  1.35  2.61 cell <- prod(vapply(axes, function(a) diff(a[1:2]), numeric(1))) c(   exact = max(lp) + log(sum(w) * cell),   `VB-corrected` = fit$logml,   Laplace = fit$logml_laplace ) #>        exact VB-corrected      Laplace  #>    -11.61846    -11.61530    -11.70894

title: Get started with inlavanilla
text: Without gradient, inla_vanilla() uses finite differences logpost. analytic gradient makes fit faster accurate, pays number parameters grows. logistic regression short: two fits agree several decimal places, gradient version calls logpost far less often. inla_vanilla() checks supplied gradient finite differences init warns disagree, catches slips hand-derived gradients.
code: grad <- function(theta, X, y) {   eta <- as.numeric(X %*% theta)   as.numeric(crossprod(X, y - plogis(eta))) - theta / 2.5^2 } fit_g <- inla_vanilla(logpost, init, grad = grad, X = X, y = y, verbose = FALSE) max(abs(fit_g$summary - fit$summary)) #> [1] 1.813245e-06 rbind(finite_differences = fit$counts, gradient = fit_g$counts) #>                    logpost grad #> finite_differences     511    0 #> gradient               127  124

title: INLA-style posterior approximation for any log-posterior — inla_vanilla
text: Approximates posterior parameter vector log density alone, using approximation pipeline INLAvaan latent field nothing model-specific. pipeline four stages: Joint Gaussian (Laplace). posterior mode \(\vartheta^*\) inverse Hessian \(\Omega\) give Gaussian approximation \(N(\vartheta^*, \Omega)\) Laplace estimate log marginal likelihood. VB mean correction. Gaussian recentred \(\tilde\vartheta = \vartheta^* + \hat\delta\), mean maximises expected log-posterior, covariance unchanged. Skew-normal marginals. parameter, log-posterior scanned along conditional mode path Gaussian, corrected changing volume parameters, fitted skew-normal \(SN(\hat\xi_j, \hat\omega_j, \hat\alpha_j)\). Gaussian copula draws. sampling() couples skew-normal marginals correlations \(\Omega\).

title: INLA-style posterior approximation for any log-posterior — inla_vanilla
code: # Normal data with unknown mean and standard deviation, on the scale # (mu, log sigma) set.seed(1) y <- rnorm(30, mean = 5, sd = 2)  logpost <- function(theta, y) {   mu <- theta[["mu"]]   sigma <- exp(theta[["log_sigma"]])   sum(dnorm(y, mu, sigma, log = TRUE)) +     dnorm(mu, 0, 10, log = TRUE) + # prior on mu     dexp(sigma, rate = 1, log = TRUE) + # prior on sigma ...     theta[["log_sigma"]] # ... and its Jacobian }  fit <- inla_vanilla(logpost, init = c(mu = 0, log_sigma = 0), y = y) #> ✔ Found the posterior mode in 10 iterations [5ms] #> ✔ VB mean correction, max shift 0.24σ [2ms] #> ✔ Fitted 2 skew-normal marginals [7ms] fit #> ── INLAvanilla ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── 20ms ── #> 2 parameters · skew-normal marginals · VB-corrected #>  #>             Mean     SD   2.5%    50%  97.5%   Mode #> mu         5.159  0.327  4.517  5.159  5.800  5.159 #> log_sigma  0.616  0.129  0.377  0.610  0.885  0.599 #>  #> Log marginal likelihood: -66.38  # The posterior of sigma itself, through the draws sigma <- sampling(fit, fun = function(theta) exp(theta[["log_sigma"]])) quantile(sigma, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)) #>     2.5%      50%    97.5%  #> 1.444354 1.832695 2.455869

title: inlavanilla: INLA-Style Skew-Normal Marginals for Any Log-Posterior — inlavanilla-package
text: Approximates posterior distribution log density alone, using approximation pipeline 'INLAvaan' package (Jamil Rue, 2026a) doi:10.48550/arXiv.2603.25690 , adaptation Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation (Rue et al., 2009) doi:10.1111/j.1467-9868.2008.00700.x , latent field nothing model-specific. Laplace approximation variational Bayes mean correction gives log marginal likelihood, skew-normal fitted parameter's marginal scanning log-posterior, Gaussian copula couples marginals posterior draws. See also Jamil Rue (2026b) doi:10.48550/arXiv.2604.00671 .

title: Draw from an approximate posterior — sampling
code: set.seed(1) y <- rnorm(30, mean = 5, sd = 2) logpost <- function(theta, y) {   sigma <- exp(theta[["log_sigma"]])   sum(dnorm(y, theta[["mu"]], sigma, log = TRUE)) +     dnorm(theta[["mu"]], 0, 10, log = TRUE) +     dexp(sigma, log = TRUE) + theta[["log_sigma"]] } fit <- inla_vanilla(logpost, c(mu = 0, log_sigma = 0), y = y, verbose = FALSE)  draws <- sampling(fit, nsamp = 2000) head(draws) #>            mu log_sigma #> [1,] 5.603356 0.5173617 #> [2,] 5.125348 0.5495693 #> [3,] 5.285843 0.5657669 #> [4,] 5.141380 0.6024758 #> [5,] 4.707959 0.8346202 #> [6,] 5.023140 0.7795313  # A derived quantity: the coefficient of variation sigma / mu cv <- sampling(fit, nsamp = 2000, fun = function(theta) {   c(cv = exp(theta[["log_sigma"]]) / theta[["mu"]]) }) quantile(cv, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)) #>      2.5%       50%     97.5%  #> 0.2716513 0.3583291 0.4832763
